raw_lines: The basic steps to integrate the ActiveX controls at document level into your application are as follows:
1.   First, instantiate MapForceControl in your application. Instantiating this control is mandatory; it
enables support for the MapForceControl Document and MapForceControl Placeholder controls
mentioned above. It is important to set the IntegrationLevel 1540 property to
ICActiveXIntegrationOnDocumentLevel (or "1"). To hide the control from the user, set its Visible
property to False. Note that, when integrating at document level, do not use the Open method of the
MapForceControl; this might lead to unexpected results. Use the corresponding open methods of
MapForceControl Document and MapForceControl PlaceHolder instead.
2.   Create at least one instance of MapForceControl Document in your application. This control supplies
the document editing window of MapForce to your application and can be instantiated multiple times if
necessary. Use the method Open to load any existing file. To access document-related functionality,
use the Path and Save or methods and properties accessible via the property Document. Note that the
control does not support a read-only mode. The value of the property ReadOnly is ignored.

When you integrate at document level, no MapForce menu or toolbar is available to your application. Instead,
you can retrieve the required commands, view their status, and execute them programmatically, as follows:
·   To retrieve all available commands, use the CommandsList 1540 property of the MapForceControl.

·   To retrieve commands organized by the toolbar in which they appear, use the Toolbars 1541 property.
·   To send commands to MapForce, use the Exec 1542 method.
·   To query if a command is currently enabled or disabled, use the QueryStatus 1543 method.
This enables you to flexibly integrate MapForce commands into your application's menus and toolbars.

folder <ApplicationFolder>\Examples\ActiveX\Images of your MapForce installation for icons in GIF format. The
file names correspond to the command names as they are listed in the Command Reference 1525 section.

The method InsertMenuStructure takes as parameters the mainMenu and the objCommand objects (the
former is the existing static menu, while the latter contains the full menu structure retrieved from the MapForce
ActiveX control). The retrieved MapForce menu structure is then merged into the existing static menu. Note that
the menus File, Project, and Window are not added dynamically. This is intentional, because these menus
deal with actively open documents, and they would require code which is beyond the scope of this example.
The basic file management commands (create, open, save, bring into focus) are handled by the existing static
menus File and Window. All other menus are inserted dynamically based on the information taken from the
MainMenu property of the ActiveX control. The new menus are inserted after "File" but before "Window", i.e.
The method InsertMenuStructure iterates through all top-level menus found in MapForceCommand object and
adds a new menu item for each. Since each top-level menu has its own child menu items, a call to the method
InsertMenuCommand takes place for each encountered child menu item. Furthermore, since each child menu
item can have its own children menu items, and so on, the InsertMenuCommand method recurses into itself
until no more child menu items exist.
The commands added dynamically are instances of the class CustomMenuItem, which is defined in
CustomMenuItem.cs. This class is derived from System.Windows.Forms.MenuItem class and has an
additional member to store the MapForce command ID.

private void AltovaMenuItem_Click(object sender, EventArgs e)
If the command is a container for other commands (that is, if it has child commands), it gets the event handler
AltovaSubMenu_Popup. This handler queries the status of each child command and enables or disables it as
required. This ensures that each command is enabled only when that is meaningful (for example, the File |
Save menu item should be disabled if there is no active document open).
The method ProcessCommand delegates the execution either to the MapForceControl itself or to any active
MapForce document loaded in a MapForceControlDocument control. This is necessary because the
MapForceControl has no way to know which document is currently active in the hosting application.

source_claims.claim: Status bit mask: bit 0/value 1 Supported, bit 1/value 2 Enabled (can execute), bit 2/value 4 Checked. Zero means invalid/unrecognized command; 1 or 5 means disabled. Client should call document-control QueryStatus if active document currently available. Other bits/values unstated.

raw_lines: QueryStatus returns the enabled/disabled and checked/unchecked status of the command specified by
nCmdID. The status is returned as a bit mask.
0           1           Supported               Set if the command is supported.
1           2           Enabled                 Set if the command is enabled (can be executed).
2           4           Checked                 Set if the command is checked.
This means that if QueryStatus returns 0 the command ID is not recognized as a valid MapForce command. If
QueryStatus returns a value of 1 or 5 the command is disabled. The client should call the QueryStatus
method of the document control if there is currently an active document available in the application.

claims.claim: The COM API enables other applications to automate MapForce tasks such as options/output. Source says MapForce follows Microsoft automation-server specifications and is registered as a COM server object during installation; registered server can be invoked from applications/scripting languages supporting COM (.NET, C++, Visual Basic, JScript, VBScript). No activation identifier, signature, bitness, apartment, license, startup/lifetime or error contract is given.

raw_lines: The COM-based API of MapForce enables other applications to use the functionality of MapForce. This makes
it possible to automate a wide range of tasks, for example, defining various options, generating output, and
The MapForce COM API follows the common specifications for automation servers as set out by Microsoft.
MapForce is automatically registered as a COM server object during installation. Once the COM server object
is registered, you can invoke it from within applications and scripting languages that have programming support
for COM calls. This makes it possible to access the MapForce API not only from development environments
using .NET, C++ and Visual Basic but also from scripting languages such as JScript and VBScript.

The basic steps to integrate the ActiveX controls at document level into your application are as follows:
1.   First, instantiate MapForceControl in your application. Instantiating this control is mandatory; it
enables support for the MapForceControl Document and MapForceControl Placeholder controls
mentioned above. It is important to set the IntegrationLevel 1540 property to

property to False. Note that, when integrating at document level, do not use the Open method of the
MapForceControl; this might lead to unexpected results. Use the corresponding open methods of
MapForceControl Document and MapForceControl PlaceHolder instead.
2.   Create at least one instance of MapForceControl Document in your application. This control supplies
the document editing window of MapForce to your application and can be instantiated multiple times if
necessary. Use the method Open to load any existing file. To access document-related functionality,
use the Path and Save or methods and properties accessible via the property Document. Note that the
control does not support a read-only mode. The value of the property ReadOnly is ignored.
3.   Optionally, add to your application the MapForceControl Placeholder control for each additional window
(other than the document window) that must be available to your application. Instances of

your application. The window kind (for example, Project window) is defined by the property
PlaceholderWindowID. Therefore, to set the window kind, set the property PlaceholderWindowID. For
valid window identifiers, see MapForceControlPlaceholderWindow 1555 . Use only one MapForceControl
For placeholder controls that select the MapForce project window, additional methods are available.

Method: QueryStatus (nCmdID as long) as long
QueryStatus returns the enabled/disabled and checked/unchecked status of the command specified by
nCmdID. The status is returned as a bit mask.
0           1           Supported               Set if the command is supported.
1           2           Enabled                 Set if the command is enabled (can be executed).
2           4           Checked                 Set if the command is checked.
This means that if QueryStatus returns 0 the command ID is not recognized as a valid MapForce command. If
QueryStatus returns a value of 1 or 5, the command is disabled.

pages.reason: This is annotated chart-config XML, not named function declarations. SettingsVersion, General, XAxis/YAxis/ZAxis, fonts, chart-kind-specific elements and gauge/color ranges remain a distinct configuration decomposition obligation; repeated Color, Size, AutoRange etc. are role-specific, not label-deduplicated. No function proposals created.

XSLT/XML/output example, not a signature catalog. Calls to create-chart-config-from-xml, create-chart-data-row, create-chart-data-series-from-rows, create-chart and save-chart-image are uses only. The example uses three arguments for create-chart; do not infer an overload from that call. Owning chart catalog is a different, excluded nonleaf page; it was not decomposed in this pass.

appendix_options.default_option_note: No separately named mode/option argument identified; exact parameter types/cardinality remain in the signature. Behavioral boundary and typed-failure cases remain unassessed.

evaluate.note: Mandatory expression string plus optional in-scope item* values for p1 through pN in numerical order; static context inherits namespaces/types/functions, base URI and default namespace, not variables.
evaluate.ambiguity: No return type in displayed signature. Variadic arity 1+ is stated by prose, not comma splitting.

encode-for-rtf.note: preserveallwhitespace and preservenewlines are independent required boolean arguments.

xbrl-footnotes.note: XSLT context only; product edition must have XBRL support. No broader backend proof.

xbrl-labels.note: QName plus taxonomy location string; XSLT and XBRL-enabled edition context.

format-duration.note: Picture argument controls output duration fields and formatting.

parse-duration.note: Input string parsed with explicit Picture argument.

add-seconds-to-time.note: Prose says seconds range 0..59.999 and shows a fractional input.
add-seconds-to-time.ambiguity: Displayed second parameter is named Minutes and typed xs:integer, while prose/example describe fractional seconds. Preserved verbatim; no corrected overload inferred.

weekday-from-date.note: One argument defaults to Sunday=1. Format=0 selects Sunday=1, every other integer Monday=1.

weekday-from-dateTime.note: One argument defaults to Sunday=1. Format=0 selects Sunday=1, every other integer Monday=1.

weeknumber-from-date.ambiguity: Displayed signature has two required-looking arguments, but default prose and a one-argument example suggest optional Calendar. Do not manufacture a separate one-argument signature.

weeknumber-from-dateTime.ambiguity: Displayed signature has two required-looking arguments, but default prose and a one-argument example suggest optional Calendar. Do not manufacture a separate one-argument signature.

build-date.note: Year/month/date integers must lie in valid ranges (month at most 12).

build-time.note: Three-argument form has no timezone; fourth string argument supplies timezone. Hours 0..23, minutes/seconds 0..59.

build-duration.note: Two-argument form builds yearMonthDuration and normalizes months >=12. Four-argument form builds dayTimeDuration and carries time units.

parse-date.note: DatePattern must match input; D/M/Y components and arbitrary separators; xs:date output lexical YYYY-MM-DD.

parse-dateTime.note: DateTimePattern has D/M/Y/H/m/s components; output lexical YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.

parse-time.note: TimePattern has H/m/s components; input order follows pattern, omitted seconds example defaults to 00.

dateTime-from-epoch.note: Epoch seconds from 1970-01-01 UTC; adjusts for local timezone and appends timezone.
dateTime-from-epoch.ambiguity: Displayed signature lacks a closing parenthesis after Epoch as xs:decimal. Single argument justified by prose, not silent signature repair.

dateTime-from-epoch-no-TZ.note: Epoch seconds; adjusts for local timezone then omits timezone suffix.
dateTime-from-epoch-no-TZ.ambiguity: Displayed signature lacks a closing parenthesis. Retain exact text; no repaired source claim.

format-geolocation.note: Output format integer 1..4: degree-minute-second plus orientation; decimal degrees plus orientation; degree-minute-second plus sign; decimal degrees plus sign. Latitude +/-90, longitude +/-180.
format-geolocation.ambiguity: Example for format=1 appears to reverse hemispheres relative to numeric inputs. Manual examples are not runtime proof.

parse-geolocation.note: Latitude then longitude separated by whitespace; six lexical forms permit mixed formats; quotes escaped by doubling.
parse-geolocation.ambiguity: Example with -22.22 longitude reports positive 22.22. Do not normalize contradictory example into proof.

geolocation-distance-km.note: Kilometers; documented geolocation lexical forms and coordinate bounds apply.

geolocation-distance-mi.note: Miles, distinct function from kilometers; same documented input lexical forms and bounds.

geolocations-bounding-rectangle.note: Sequence of input geolocations; output format 1..4; prose says two strings for top-left and bottom-right.
geolocations-bounding-rectangle.ambiguity: Displayed xs:sequence argument and xs:string return disagree with conventional type spelling/prose two-string result. Preserve instead of correcting.

geolocation-within-polygon.note: Two argument positions: point and sequence of polygon points; automatically closes polygon if final point differs from first. Nested + denotes polygon-point multiplicity, not a family to split.
geolocation-within-polygon.ambiguity: Nonstandard nested parameter notation; arity 2 is supported by the prose/examples, not by a conventional type declaration.

geolocation-within-rectangle.note: Point plus two opposite rectangle corners; input lexical forms and coordinate bounds apply.

suggested-image-file-extension.note: Base64 image; suggestion from embedded type, empty string if unavailable.

image-exif-data.note: Base64 JPEG -> Exif element with standard/vendor tags and derived Geolocation/OrientationDegree. Orientation translation 1/8/3/6 -> 0/90/180/270; no translation for 2/4/5/7. Tag labels are attributes, not functions.
image-exif-data.unresolved: Entire standard/vendor-specific Exif attribute behavior is not separately atomized.

generate-auto-number.note: ID names counter; StartsWith initial number, Increment each call; ResetOnChange change resets counter. Explicit reset is separate function.

reset-auto-number.note: Resets named counter to its original StartsWith.
reset-auto-number.ambiguity: No return type supplied by displayed signature; do not infer empty-sequence().

schema.note: Distinct 0-argument whole-schema role and 2-argument component-kind/QName role return navigation functions. Imported schema is required. Component/property records are not further function declarations.
schema.unresolved: Schema component/property-name and property-type tables remain nested behavior obligations; no blind expansion of table labels.

type.note: Element/attribute PSVI type; XML must declare schema. Returned function accepts property names, including _props.
type.ambiguity: Signature says item? rather than item()?; retain verbatim. Component/property tables not atomized.

attributes.note: Attribute axis, default local-name case-sensitive. SearchOptions r=regex, f=full rather than partial match, i=case-insensitive, p=include namespace prefix; any order, invalid flags error, empty string allowed, empty sequence disallowed.

elements.note: Child element axis, not attribute axis. Flags r/f/i/p; any order, invalid flags error, empty string allowed, empty sequence disallowed.

find-first.note: Condition is arity-1 boolean predicate; stop at first matching item.
find-first.ambiguity: Displayed signature has unconventional nested predicate notation. Do not equate to a scalar builtin by local name.

find-first-combination.note: Condition arity 2; Cartesian ordered pairs, not aligned positional pairs; returns first match or no items.

find-first-pair.note: Condition arity 2; aligned pairs (X1,Y1),(X2,Y2)..., not Cartesian pairs.

find-first-pair-pos.note: Aligned pairs; return index position of first match, or no results.
find-first-pair-pos.ambiguity: Signature return is xs:integer, while prose allows no result. Preserve this uncertainty.

find-first-pos.note: Arity-1 boolean predicate; return first matching item index; examples use one-based indexing.

for-each-attribute-pair.note: Alphabetical same-name attribute pairing includes disjoint pairs; apply function to each pair.

for-each-combination.note: Apply third-argument function to Cartesian combinations in first-then-second sequence order.
for-each-combination.ambiguity: Signature embeds a sample inline Function($i,$j){$i || $j}, not a conventional function type. Do not turn $i/$j into outer parameters.

for-each-matching-attribute-pair.note: Alphabetical same-name attribute pairing omits disjoint pairs, unlike for-each-attribute-pair.

substitute-empty.note: Use second sequence only when first is empty.
substitute-empty.ambiguity: SecondSequence signature says item() but examples pass multiple items. No silent cardinality correction.

camel-case.note: One argument uses whitespace regex. Three arguments use SplitChars as regex if IsRegex true, otherwise literal characters; first output character capitalized.

char.note: One argument reads string-converted context item; two arguments read explicit string. Missing/negative position examples yield empty string.

create-hash-from-string.note: Default SHA-256; optional HashAlgo MD5, SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, case-insensitive.

first-chars.note: One-argument context-item form distinct from explicit-string two-argument form; examples allow counts exceeding length.

format-string.note: %1/%2/... substituted using format sequence; missing value preserves placeholder.

last-chars.note: One-argument context-item form distinct from explicit-string two-argument form; examples allow counts exceeding length.

pad-string-left.note: Required pad character is one character; pad only if requested length exceeds current length, otherwise unchanged; multi-character pad error shown.

pad-string-right.note: Right-padding role distinct from left; required pad character single character; length <= current length leaves unchanged.

substring-after-last.note: Use last occurrence; missing match -> empty string, empty needle -> entire main string.

substring-before-last.note: Use last occurrence; missing or empty needle -> empty string (different empty-needle role from after-last).

substring-pos.note: One-based index, 0 when absent. Third argument sets search start but returned index stays relative to entire string.

decode-string.note: Default UTF-8; documented encodings US-ASCII, ISO-8859-1, UTF-16/LE/BE, ISO-10646-UCS2, UTF-32/LE/BE, ISO-10646-UCS4.

encode-string.note: Default UTF-8; text says initially UTF-8 only and other encodings will be added. Do not promote the future list to current support.
encode-string.ambiguity: Both signatures print xs:base64Binaryinteger; preserve malformed return type. Encoding scope differs from decode-string.

get-temp-folder.note: Current user's temporary folder; environment-dependent, no fixed Windows path inferred.

high-res-timer.note: System high-resolution timer in seconds, system availability/resolution dependent.

parse-html.note: String may omit HTML root; returned tree root named HTML; valid input recommended.

sleep.note: Suspend current operation for required integer milliseconds; empty-sequence() return.

same_label_review.name: parse-date
same_label_review.reason: Core conversion library, Built-in/C++/C#/Java, delegates format semantics to its parse-dateTime; appendix expanded QName is Altova XPath/XQuery extension with DatePattern grammar and language badges. No documented alias equates the identities or preserves every format contract.

same_label_review.name: parse-dateTime
same_label_review.reason: Core format-mask catalog includes d/h/P/f and presentation specifiers, while appendix explicitly lists D/M/Y/H/m/s DateTimePattern. They have different documented surfaces/language contexts, not verified equivalent signatures.

same_label_review.name: parse-time
same_label_review.reason: Core uses core parse-dateTime format semantics and native/managed backends; appendix is explicit Altova extension TimePattern in XPath/XQuery. No alias proof.

same_label_review.name: age
same_label_review.reason: Core optional now parameter overlaps both appendix roles (system date or explicit date), but is a separate library surface with Built-in/C++/C#/Java eligibility. Preserve both appendix signatures and the existing leaf; do not claim independent additive behavior or merge eligibility.

same_label_review.name: type
same_label_review.reason: SPL Type is a code-generator object representing types; altova:type is a PSVI query returning a property-navigation function. Case-folded label equality is not semantic equality.

same_label_review.name: pad-string-left
same_label_review.reason: Existing lang-library desired-length is xs:int; appendix StringLength is xs:integer with explicit no-padding and pad-error cases. No expanded-QName alias or full lexical/backend equivalence established.

same_label_review.name: pad-string-right
same_label_review.reason: Existing lang-library desired-length is xs:int; appendix StringLength is xs:integer. Preserve right-padding role and surface context; no alias/equivalence proof.

same_label_review.name: repeat-string
same_label_review.reason: Core/lang count type xs:int differs from appendix Repeats xs:integer; native/managed and XPath/XQuery contexts are different exposed surfaces. No alias proof, no additive behavior claim.

same_label_review.name: sleep
same_label_review.reason: Existing sleep takes data plus fractional seconds and passes data through, delaying each sequence item; altova:sleep takes integer milliseconds, suspends current operation and returns empty-sequence(). Never merge by name.

appendix_identity_boundaries.negative_limits: Other existing objects receive no exact-member match, not a proof of semantic disjointness. Source-file/QName/signature/context comparisons preserve originals and every same-label alternative. No issue ownership follows from overlap or from these broad rows.

same_label_decisions.name: parse-date
same_label_decisions.reason: Core conversion library, Built-in/C++/C#/Java, delegates format semantics to its parse-dateTime; appendix expanded QName is Altova XPath/XQuery extension with DatePattern grammar and language badges. No documented alias equates the identities or preserves every format contract.

same_label_decisions.name: parse-dateTime
same_label_decisions.reason: Core format-mask catalog includes d/h/P/f and presentation specifiers, while appendix explicitly lists D/M/Y/H/m/s DateTimePattern. They have different documented surfaces/language contexts, not verified equivalent signatures.

same_label_decisions.name: parse-time
same_label_decisions.reason: Core uses core parse-dateTime format semantics and native/managed backends; appendix is explicit Altova extension TimePattern in XPath/XQuery. No alias proof.

same_label_decisions.name: age
same_label_decisions.reason: Core optional now parameter overlaps both appendix roles (system date or explicit date), but is a separate library surface with Built-in/C++/C#/Java eligibility. Preserve both appendix signatures and the existing leaf; do not claim independent additive behavior or merge eligibility.

same_label_decisions.name: pad-string-left
same_label_decisions.reason: Existing lang-library desired-length is xs:int; appendix StringLength is xs:integer with explicit no-padding and pad-error cases. No expanded-QName alias or full lexical/backend equivalence established.

same_label_decisions.name: pad-string-right
same_label_decisions.reason: Existing lang-library desired-length is xs:int; appendix StringLength is xs:integer. Preserve right-padding role and surface context; no alias/equivalence proof.

same_label_decisions.name: repeat-string
same_label_decisions.reason: Core/lang count type xs:int differs from appendix Repeats xs:integer; native/managed and XPath/XQuery contexts are different exposed surfaces. No alias proof, no additive behavior claim.

same_label_decisions.name: sleep
same_label_decisions.reason: Existing sleep takes data plus fractional seconds and passes data through, delaying each sequence item; altova:sleep takes integer milliseconds, suspends current operation and returns empty-sequence(). Never merge by name.
